claims.title: Independent latent-model counts satisfy an exact multinomial second-moment TV bound
claims.scope: N independent categorical latent-model draws over k observed labels
assumptions: draws are iid from one stationary categorical law
nonclaims: lower-level repeated observations within one persistent latent unit are not counted as independent latent draws

claims.title: Markov calibration gives a finite-sample TV confidence radius from independent latent-model draws
claims.scope: the same fixed-sample iid categorical design at failure probability alpha
assumptions: rho squared is at least (k-1)/(4N alpha)
nonclaims: the conservative radius is not claimed optimal

claims.title: The fixed-sample latent-prior confidence radius can be rounded outward exactly on a rational grid
claims.scope: nonnegative rational squared-radius targets and a declared positive integer grid denominator
nonclaims: grid rounding does not improve the underlying statistical bound

claims.title: Independent-latent confidence balls compose with Bayesian value and marginal-gain TV sensitivity bounds
claims.scope: confidence event TV(p,p_hat)<=rho combined with the Bayesian Boolean prior-robustness lane
assumptions: the prior-robust value and gain Lipschitz theorems apply to the downstream decision problem
nonclaims: confidence-set coverage does not imply the nominal prior is the true data-generating prior

claims.title: The effective sample size for mixing-weight calibration is the number of independent latent draws, not within-unit observation count
claims.scope: hierarchical models distinguishing iid latent units from repeated conditional observations of one persistent latent state
assumptions: the confidence theorem is applied only to counts of independent latent labels
nonclaims: within-unit observations may still identify the unit's latent model

claims.title: Bounded exact independent-latent confidence audit
claims.scope: outward square-root rounding, confidence radii, sample-size scaling, full-simplex clipping, downstream value/gain bands, and ranking certificates
assumptions: all count arithmetic and downstream bounds use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded tests are not an empirical validation of simulation hypotheses
CI success is not evidence for simulation
